workload-generator.stdout:
Obj-A Workload Generator

Generates a sorted synthetic workload in the CSV format used by Obj-B.

Usage:
  ./workload-generator --out <file> --interval <start,end>
                       --distribution <uniform|normal|geometric|poisson>
                       <distribution statistics> [options]

Distribution statistics:
  uniform:   --min <integer> --max <integer>
  normal:    --mean <number> --stddev <positive number>
  geometric: --probability <number in (0,1]>
  poisson:   --lambda <positive number>

Task options:
  --tasks-per-job <count>          Number of tasks in each generated job. Default: 1
  --task-work <fixed|distribution> Fixed work or work drawn from the same distribution.
                                    Default: fixed
  --fixed-task-work <positive N>   W N value used by fixed task work. Default: 10

Other options:
  --seed <integer>                 Reproduce the same random workload.
  --job-prefix <text>              Prefix for job IDs. Default: j
  --help                           Show this help text.

Examples:
  ./workload-generator --out workload.csv --interval 0,20 \
      --distribution uniform --min 0 --max 2 \
      --tasks-per-job 2 --task-work fixed --fixed-task-work 10 --seed 7

  ./workload-generator --out workload.csv --interval 0,50 \
      --distribution poisson --lambda 1.5 \
      --tasks-per-job 1 --task-work distribution --seed 42

workload-generator.stderr:

Run workload-generator --help for usage.

workload-visualizer.stdout:
Obj-A Workload Visualizer

Creates a PNG histogram or scatter plot from a workload CSV file.

Usage:
  ./workload-visualizer <workload.csv> --hist="arrival time" --out=plot.png [options]
  ./workload-visualizer <workload.csv> --scat="arrival time,len(Tasks)" --out=plot.png [options]

Plot modes:
  --hist <column>              Histogram of one numeric column.
  --scat <x-column,y-column>   Scatter plot comparing two numeric columns.

Supported numeric workload values:
  arrival time
  len(Tasks)

Options:
  --out <file.png>             Output PNG file. Required.
  --bins <count>               Histogram bin count. Default: 10
  --xlim <min,max>             Optional x-axis limits.
  --ylim <min,max>             Optional y-axis limits.
  --title <text>               Optional plot title.
  --width <pixels>             PNG width. Default: 1000
  --height <pixels>            PNG height. Default: 700
  --help                       Show this help text.

Examples:
  ./workload-visualizer workload.csv \
      --hist="arrival time" --bins=20 --out=arrival-histogram.png

  ./workload-visualizer workload.csv \
      --scat="arrival time,len(Tasks)" \
      --title="Arrival Time vs Task Count" \
      --out=arrival-vs-tasks.png

workload-visualizer.stderr:

simple-queue-sim.stdout:
Usage: simple-queue-sim CONFIG [TIME_LIMIT] [--time-limit N] [--metrics FILE] [--events FILE]

Simulates exactly one queue-system row from CONFIG. Source/sink paths in the
configuration are resolved relative to CONFIG. If no time limit is given, the
simulator runs until all source jobs have arrived and the queue/servers drain.
